name: Code style
content:
# Code style

Use this when writing or changing code in someone else's repository.

## Match the codebase

- Read neighboring files first and copy their naming, structure, error handling, and test style.
- Follow the repo's linters, formatters, and contributor docs (CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md).
- Use the libraries the project already uses. Add a dependency only when the task needs it, and say so.

## Keep the change small

- Change only what the task needs. No drive-by refactors, renames, or reformatting.
- One concept per function and file. Prefer clear names over comments.
- Comments explain why, never what. No commented-out or dead code.

## Correctness

- Validate input at boundaries (HTTP, CLI, files, external APIs).
- Handle errors where you can act on them; otherwise let them surface with context.
- Never log or commit secrets. Keep credentials in the environment.
- Add or update tests with every behavior change, next to the code they cover.

## Before you finish

- Run the project's checks (format, lint, type check, tests) when you can.
- Re-read your diff as a reviewer would: remove debug output and unrelated edits.
- Write a commit message with an imperative summary, then what changed and why.
